documents.name: Orientation.md
documents.text:
# Field session handbook
## Stride session
The Stride session includes a river crossing. Read the Foot protection section of Equipment.md for the equipment rules. This orientation gives the purpose of the session rather than a packing list.
## Recording observations
Teams write the observation time and the stop name before recording what they see. Separate direct observations from interpretations. If a detail was not observed, leave that field blank and explain the gap rather than copying another team's entry. The organiser reviews legibility before the sheets are archived. This is a procedure for documenting the session, not a statement about the natural history of the site.
## Working in groups
Each group selects a recorder and a route reader. Swap these roles at the halfway stop so that everyone has an opportunity to practise both activities. A group should stay together between the marked stops. Tell the session leader before leaving the group. The orientation does not identify a particular person as leader; names are announced at the meeting point.
## Looking after records
Use the printed stop identifiers consistently so that sheets from different teams can be compared. When correcting a copied identifier, keep the old entry readable and add the correction beside it. Do not rewrite another team's observations. The records should describe the trip that actually occurred rather than a planned route that was not followed.
## End of session
At the final stop, check that every sheet has the date and a group identifier. Return borrowed clipboards to the collection box. Keep personal notes separate from the sheets being returned. The organiser will collect questions about observations for a later discussion, but this orientation does not schedule that discussion or promise a publication date.
## Reading the other documents
Different documents have different purposes. The equipment sheet supplies practical requirements; the orientation explains the recording process. A missing detail on this page does not imply that the corresponding requirement is absent from the equipment sheet. Follow an explicit reference to a relevant section before treating that detail as unknown. The Lantern festival and the shelf-loan notice describe separate activities with separate rules.

documents.name: Equipment.md
documents.text:
# Equipment
## Foot protection
Closed shoes are compulsory. Sandals are prohibited. The supplied overshoes go over the participant's own closed shoes; they do not replace them.
## Shared kit
The leader supplies clipboards. A personal camera is optional. Return borrowed kit at the final collection box.

documents.text:
# Lantern festival — current 2026 notice
This guide replaces the archived notice.
## Admission and workshop
Visitor admission is free. The lantern workshop has seven places and costs five credits per place. Booking a workshop place is separate from entering the festival.
## Meeting point
Workshop participants meet at East Pavilion at 16:20 on 9 November 2026.
## Missing information
The notice names no sponsor and provides no weather forecast.

# Lantern festival — archived 2025 notice
This obsolete notice offered fourteen workshop places. Its meeting point was West Lodge. The current notice replaces these instructions.

documents.name: Paper sculpture.md
documents.text:
# A loop sculpture
## Assembly
Fold each of six paper strips into a loop and join neighbouring loops using clips. Arrange the connected loops on a flat surface.
## Limits
The directions describe assembly but supply no dimensions, material masses or final weight. No measurement method for weight is specified.

documents.name: Shelf loan notice.md
documents.text:
# Shelf loan notice
Printed novels can be borrowed for 15 days. One renewal is allowed only if nobody else has reserved the book. A reservation prevents renewal even if the book is not overdue. Reference maps remain in the reading room. This notice does not state a fine for late returns.
